blocks.title: Introduction and description of results
blocks.content:
Introduction and description of results
This paper is about knots which are transverse to the standard tight contact structure in
R3, and about the ways in which topological information about braids can be used to
learn new things about these ‘transversal knots’. Our approach to contact topology had
its origins in the foundational paper of D Bennequin [2]. The results in this paper are
direct outgrowths of our work on the Markov Theorem without Stabilization (MTWS)
[6].

JOAN S BIRMAN

The main result of this paper is a negative answer to the question: are all transversal
knot types transversally simple? An explicit inﬁnite family of examples is given of
closed 3–braids that deﬁne transversal knot types that are not transversally simple.
The method of proof is topological and indirect.

blocks.title: Markov’s Theorem Without Stabilization [6]
blocks.content: Let X be an oriented knot type and let (X+, X−) be a pair of closed braids such that X−∈Bmin(X) and X+ ∈B(X) with b(X+) = m and b(X−) = n. Then there exist X′ + ∈B(X), X′ −∈Bmin(X), and a ﬁnite set of templates T (m, n) (whose membership is only dependent on (m, n)) such that: (1) X+ is exchange reducible to X′ + and X−is exchange equivalent to X′ −, and (2) There is a template (D+, D−) in the ﬁnite set T (m, n) where, using the same braiding assignment, on D+ and D−, the diagram D+ carries X′ + and the diagram D−carries X′ −.

blocks.title: The Bennequin Trick
blocks.content: Let Γ ⊂R3 be an oriented differentiable graph that is transversal to the standard contact structure ξ of R3. Let e ⊂Γ be an edge having a local parameterization function f(t): [0, 1] →R3 where f(t) = (ρ(t), θ(t), z(t)). If dθ dt is not positive for all t then there exists a transversal isotopy of Γ which is the identity everywhere except on a small neighborhood of e such that for a resulting parameterization bf(t) = (bρ(t), bθ(t),bz(t)) we have dbθ dt being everywhere positive.
